facts.value: Small-scale CSA2 config derived for the p1 model (task ae-2, V4.1 Step 0; corrected after 3b's PR #213 review): L=12, d=1024, heads=8, MoE 48/top-3/1-shared with expert_ffn=1728 (ffn_hidden=6912 under the existing equal-active parity), giving 352.3M active params/token (33.6M tied embedding + 318.8M layers) and 3.22B total (name 3.2b-a352m-e48). Per-layer attention params per paper Fig. 4: only Full computes Main K/V -- S = 4d^2 (Q + SWA K/V/O), F = 7d^2 + idx, X = 5d^2 + idx, R = 5d^2 (Main KV and Top-K reused). CSA2: m=8 tokens/entry, top_k=64, n_win=128, indexer 4 heads x 64 dim (latent 256 = d//4). Mode placement composes with PR #216 (0e-2): n_swa_only_layers=2 owns the first-two pure-SWA placement in HybridLM's kind loop, and csa2_modes="F,R,R,R,X,R,R,R,R,R" owns the ten non-SWA layers: layer 2 Full, eight Reuse, and one X at layer 6 that is Reindex-DEFERRED (fb ruling 2026-09-10): Step 2 ships Full/Reuse only, so the module runs X as Reuse until Reindex lands; the slot names the mid-stack selection refresh point rather than a live mode. Global KV = 512 B/token (one Full layer, 4096 B/entry amortized over m=8, bf16) vs 49,152 B/token dense at the same width (12 layers x 2 x d x 2 B) -- 96x smaller. top_k is not effectively dense: 640 keys/query (64x8 + 128) = 15.6% of dense 4096, and the indexer discards 87.5% of the 512 scored entries before attention; indexer cost 131K MACs/query = 3.1% of dense QK. At top_k=128 the attended fraction is 28.1% -- 64 is the default, 128 the A/B ceiling.
facts.source: python3 scripts/v41_size.py (this commit); arithmetic printed by the script, which asserts every constraint above and fails loud if one stops holding. Corrected 2026-09-10 after 3b's changes-requested review on PR #213 (Reuse/Reindex save 2d^2 by reusing Main KV)

config.paper_values_that_do_not_transfer: 32 indexer heads x 128, 64 core heads x 512, latent 1280, top_k 512, m=2 encoder/1 decoder, 40 layers, n_win 128 -- all 552B / seq 64K-1M (DeepSeek_V41_Tech_Report.pdf section 2)
config.what_is_borrowed_not_derived: L=12 was a gap-map suggestion (fb, 2026-09-10; the gap map was a workflow agent's output, not a committed file -- confirmed by fb 2026-09-10 -- so the actual basis is this derivation from the report plus the 352.3M budget); n_win=128 (paper value, Step 3 A/Bs 128 vs 256); MoE 48/top-3/1-shared (pivot ruling, reuse MoEFFN as-is)
config.active_param_equation: per layer per Fig. 4: S = 4d^2 + ffn (Q + SWA K/V/O), F = 7d^2 + idx + ffn (adds Main K/V/O), X = 5d^2 + idx + ffn, R = 5d^2 + ffn (Main KV and Top-K reused); idx = 2*d*256 on F/X; ffn = 4*3*d*1728; embedding d*32784 once, tied head. ffn_hidden=6912 is the parity reference only -- all 12 layers are MoE, so it adds no active params
config.kv_bytes_equation: dense = LAYERS * 2 * d * 2 B = 49,152 B/token; CSA2 = Full_layers * 2 * d * 2 B / m = 512 B/token; X/R layers store no global KV
config.density_equation: attended keys/query = top_k*m + n_win = 640; entries/layer = T/m = 512; selectivity = top_k/entries = 12.5%
config.ffn_hidden_consequence: fb ruling 2026-09-10: do NOT relax MoEFFN's equal-active parity check -- set ffn_hidden = (top_k+shared)*expert_ffn = 6912 so the config stays within the check; de wires the value in Step 1
config.review_correction: 3b's changes-requested review on PR #213 found the first version counted R and X at 7d^2 (Main K/V computed per layer); the correct count is 5d^2 (Main KV reused), an overcount of 2d^2 x 9 reuse-family layers = 18.87M. At expert_ffn=1536 the corrected count was 324.0M, 26M under target; expert_ffn=1728 restores 352.3M. The assertion band tightened from 300-400M to 340-360M so the class is caught next time. (3b's review quoted 321.9M, which assumes 10 overcounted layers; the map has 9.)
config.composition_with_pr216: 0e-2 (PR #216) puts PureSWA + n_swa_only_layers in HybridLM's kind loop; this derivation's S,S prefix is owned by that field (n_swa_only_layers=2) and csa2_modes owns only the ten non-SWA layers. Open divergence flagged to 0e and de: PR #216's PureSWA reads cfg.csa_window (default 256) while de-103's CSA2 module reads csa2_n_win (128) -- one model must have one SWA width, so PureSWA should read csa2_n_win when the CSA2 module lands.
config.swa_kv_caveat: SWA KV is stored uncompressed at the gate (49,152 B/token); bounded replay (Step 7) is what makes the persistent total small, and it is deferred past the gate

facts.uncertainty: Derivation, not a measurement: the param and byte counts are exact given the assumptions; the assumptions themselves (Q shared, separate KV/O per branch, one Full serving nine Reuse layers, expert_ffn as the active-budget knob) are untested at this scale. The paper runs one Full per ~17 reuse layers at 552B; one per nine here is conservative. m=8 vs m=4 and top_k=64 vs 128 are start values in fb's ranges, not fitted optima. The Reuse/Reindex param count (5d^2) is 3b's correction of the first version's 7d^2.
facts.boundary: Holds at d=1024, L=12, seq 4096, bf16. facts.value: Bytes of the materialised attention scores in the EAGER CSA2/SWA forward, T=4096, H=8, L=12, CSA2 m=8: every CSA2 layer forms full = qh@kh^T (B,H,T,T) plus the concatenated softmax tensor (B,H,T,NB+T), and each of the 2 PureSWA layers also forms (B,H,T,T) eagerly; that is ~12 full T x T score matrices live along the forward without grad checkpointing. Dense full-score materialisation: per layer bf16 4.00 GiB at B=16, 2.00 at B=8, 1.00 at B=4, 0.50 at B=2; x12 layers: 48/24/12/6 GiB bf16 (96/48/24/12 GiB fp32 softmax workspace). Compressed-entry scores B x H x T x (T/m): 0.50/0.25/0.125/0.062 GiB per layer bf16, 6/3/1.5/0.75 GiB x12. The full-window term dominates >8:1. Against 95.22 GiB and the ~18.2 GiB MoE fixed terms, no B>=4 fits eager even dense (dense B=16 OOMed at 94.13); only B=2 fits (25.2 GiB measured peak). The compiled path is the fix: flash/SDPA attention never materialises T x T scores, after which this table ceases to describe training memory.

facts.value: ADOPT/SKIP ruling for external MoE kernels on the p1 V4.1 stack (H20 = SM90, torch 2.11.0+cu129, d=1024, 48 experts, top-3 + 1 shared, expert_ffn=1728, seq 4096, batch 4-8). SKIP both on H20 as of 2026-09-11, decided by CPU/API reading before any card time: (1) DeepGEMM 'Mega MoE' and 'Mega Gate' (PR #432, merged 2026-09-10, v2.6.1->2.80) ship ONLY sm100_* kernel implementations (csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm100_bf16_mega_gate.hpp, sm100_bf16_mega_moe.hpp, sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe.hpp; deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm100_*.cuh), gated __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 1000 with Blackwell UMMA/TMA descriptors; no sm90 variant exists. Their Hopper coverage stops at the older m_grouped_* GEMMs, the same op class as our torch._grouped_mm. Mega MoE additionally mandates multi-process symmetric memory (PyTorch >= 2.9; single-rank size==1 path exists but is a rendezvous no-op). The claimed ~20% faster MoE backward and 30-75% Mega Gate gains do not transfer to SM90. (2) deepseek-ai/tilekernels (TileLang 0.1.14 present on the pod) DOES support SM90, but tile_kernels/moe/ is routing/dispatch/combine primitives only (topk_gate, get_fused_mapping, expand_to_fused, reduce_fused, aux_fi, group_count, inplace_unique_group_indices, normalize_weight): there is no expert grouped GEMM (that is DeepGEMM's layer), and the only autograd gate wrapper, modeling/engram/engram_gate.py (EngramGateFn), computes sigmoid(signed_sqrt(dot(RMSNorm(x),RMSNorm(k)))) — a different routing function from our fp32 softmax + selection-only expert_bias MoEFFN gate, so no drop-in and no direct bit-parity. The routing primitives remain a candidate for a future microbenchmark of the dispatch chain alone; neither package can replace model.MoEFFN end-to-end on H20, so no wrapper work is justified. The pod already carries sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.0+cu129 with the mega Python bindings, consistent with the source reading (kernels absent at runtime for SM90).

facts.value: CSA2 joint entries+window via two flash calls joined by fp32 LSE (de-108) is numerically exact vs the materialized one-softmax path and removes the B8 materialized OOM, but every flash form tried today is slower than materialized; gate run stays materialized (fits at B4), de-108 is post-gate. PARITY (10 CSA2 layers d=1024 h=8 hd=128 m=8 top_k=64 n_win=128 4 indexer heads/dim64 T=512 B=2 bf16 fixed H20): fwd maxabs 1.953e-3 (rel 5.65e-3); single-layer grads dq/dk 1.22e-4, all param grads 0.3-1.0e-2 rel; CPU float64 fwd+every grad <=1.1e-15. RAGGED (one varlen entries call per indexer group, boolean-compress to true n_sel): B4 20.45 GiB/1612ms/10166 tok/s vs materialized 38.05 GiB/502ms/32670; B8 31.83 GiB/2252ms/14552 vs materialized 76.01 GiB/978ms/33500 -- halves B8 memory, 2.3-3.2x slower. RECTANGULAR collapse (uniform max_e=64 slots per query + seqused_k, one dense call/group) REJECTED: grads diverged (worst 5.1e3 vs 0.125; zero-selection queries make empty-key flash segments corrupting entries dq/dke), B4 52.87 GiB/9823ms/1668, B8 OOM; padding every query to 64 keys dominates. Exact split backward: flash_attn.cute _flash_attn_bwd subtracts within-branch g.o_j internally, so external dlse must be cross-branch c_j*(g.o_j - g.y) (None exact only standalone, c_j*g.y double-subtracts); dkw/dke 1.9e-6 vs materialized on an isolated two-branch kernel test.

facts.value: CSA2 with the ENTRIES branch kept materialized and only the SWA-window branch run on flash (de-109, cfg.csa2_win_flash) matches the single materialized softmax to the bf16 kernel floor and is 3.2-3.3x faster than materialized while fitting B8, removing the materialized path's B8 pressure. Dense selected-entry scores are only B,H,T,NB (NB=T/m=512); the materialized cost is the B,H,T,T window score tensor, so flashing the window alone captures the win with no ragged gather or per-group call. PARITY (10 CSA2 layers d=1024 h=8 hd=128 m=8 top_k=64 n_win=128 4 indexer heads/dim64 T=512 B=2 bf16 fixed H20): fwd maxabs 1.953e-3 (rel 5.65e-3, identical to de-108); worst param-grad abs 7.8e-2 (bf16 floor; CPU float64 forward and every q/k/v/x + parameter gradient <=1e-15); indexer_q and ik_weight STE grads nonzero on both paths. MEMORY/SPEED (T=4096 bf16 fwd+backward): B4 win-flash 13.11 GiB / 152.9 ms / 107,148 tok/s vs materialized 38.05 GiB / 495.0 ms / 33,101 (3.24x faster, 2.9x less memory); B8 win-flash 26.15 GiB / 292.3 ms / 112,114 tok/s vs materialized 76.01 GiB / 976.6 ms / 33,554 (3.34x faster, fits). Mechanism: one flash_attn.cute varlen causal window call (window_size=(n_win-1,0)) per layer over all heads; entries stay eager oe=(pe*ste)@vc (matmul, no B,H,T,NB,D tensor); the two branches combine by fp32 LSE and autograd supplies the window dlse=c_w(g.ow-g.y) cross term. A first form that materialized pe*vc as B,H,T,NB,D fp32 OOMed at B4 (>=17 TiB); the matmul form is the measured one.

facts.value: Why csa2_win_flash (de-109) is 3.2x faster on the CSA2 attention module but only ~1.1x faster on the full smoke step: the flashed SWA window is a negligible fraction of step COMPUTE. Analytic per-token forward FLOPs from the gate dims (L=12 d=1024 NB=512 n_win=128, scripts/de109/step_cost_breakdown.py): MoE FFN (4 active of 48 experts, SwiGLU gate+up+down, 4*3*d*1728 per layer) 509.6M = 77.3%; GatedMLA MLA projections 94.4M = 14.3% (NOT four d->d matmuls: kv_down d->d/4, kv_up d/4->2d fused k|v, qg d->2d fused q|gate, o d->d = 3.75 d^2/layer, latent KV compression per model.py GatedMLA); indexer+RMSNorm+router+embedding ~41.9M = 6.4%; dense selected-entry scores 2*NB*d x10 layers = 10.5M = 1.6%; the SWA window scores that the flag moves to flash = 2*n_win*d x12 = 3.15M = 0.48%. So the flag speeds <1% of FLOPs. Its measured pre-flag TIME share inferred by Amdahl S=1/(1-f+f/s): with attention-module speedup s=3.2 and the observed full-step S=1.11, f=0.144 (the window occupied ~14% of pre-flag step wall-time). The ~30x gap between 0.48% FLOP share and 14% time share is because the materialized path built a B,H,T,T fp32 window score tensor plus the T*T causal/document mask per layer -- write/launch/memory-bandwidth bound, not compute; flash removes that allocation (peak 43.5 vs 72.6 GiB in smoke j) without reducing arithmetic. The other 86% of step time -- MoE grouped-mm + token dispatch, Q/K/V/O projections, the dense entries matmul and eager ce/cw combine (compile does not fuse it), fp8 casts, optimizer, embedding/IO -- is unchanged by the flag. The 1.4x smoke criterion would require f=0.416, i.e. attention would have to be 42% of step time, contradicted by the FLOP accounting; 1.11x at acceptance is the expected order, not an underdelivery. Post-gate: recover more of the attention time by torch.compile-fusing the entries matmul + ce/cw split combine, which stay eager and per-layer.

facts.uncertainty: FLOP split is architecture-exact for the listed linear/score terms; the 'other' bucket (indexer/norms/router/embedding) is approximate and excludes activation, fp8 cast, dispatch/communication and optimizer FLOPs, so MoE's true time share is at least the value shown. f=0.144 is an Amdahl inference from a single noisy step-speedup point, not a CUDA profile; the 1.11x acceptance speedup compares j world4 to i world8 (different tokens/step), so f is an order-of-magnitude bound. A real per-kernel timeline on one fixed shape is the required post-gate confirmation.
